label: copy phase, late (recall_idx>=3), fed-back input in {0,1,z,x,e,c,f}
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (never during original tokens or on <DEL>), almost entirely from the 4th output onward (recall_idx>=3; rate peaks at recall_idx 4 and absolute t 11-13). It is strongly token-selective on the fed-back input: 0 (37% of mass, 10x lift), then 1, z, x, then e, c, f; it is near-silent for inputs such as o, w, h, 2. The rate rises with L and with the number of digits in the sequence, and the strongest activations (input 0) sit in runs of these preferred tokens (e.g. c 0 z, 1 0 e). The predicate covers ~94% of activation mass but has low precision (~15%): most copy-phase steps with these inputs stay below threshold, and adding context conditions (count of preferred tokens seen, preferred neighbours) raised precision only to ~25-33% at a large cost in recall. What gates the remaining selectivity was not found.
